records.source: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἶδεν τοὺς βάλλοντας εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν πλουσίους.
records.gloss: Having looked up now he saw the ones casting into the treasury the gifts of them, rich [people].
pieces: Jesus looked up and watched as rich people dropped their gifts into the temple's offering chests.

L.1: And looking up, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.

R.1: Jesus looked up. He saw rich people putting their gifts of money into the offering boxes in the temple.

decisions.choice: the treasury: the place in the temple courts where gifts for the temple were received, with chests to put them in
alternatives: a locked storeroom for the temple's money
decisions.reason: Jesus was teaching in the temple (20:1; 21:37). The treasury was in a court open to the people, where Jesus also taught (John 8:20), and gifts were dropped into chests there in full view (Mark 12:41).

decisions.choice: rich: the word stands last for emphasis: the givers Jesus watched were rich
alternatives: the rich as the only givers
decisions.reason: Luke holds the word back to the end of the sentence. It sets up the contrast with the poor widow in 21:2.

decisions.choice: the temple's offering chests (B); the offering boxes in the temple (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the treasury was, as the meaning decision explains, and name Jesus for clarity.

records.heading: A poor widow's gift

records.source: εἶδεν δέ τινα χήραν πενιχρὰν βάλλουσαν ἐκεῖ λεπτὰ δύο, καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα ἡ πτωχὴ αὕτη πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν·
records.gloss: He saw then a certain widow needy casting there lepta two, \v 3 and he said, Truly I say to you that the widow, the poor this, more than all has cast in;
pieces: He also noticed a needy widow drop in {{units:two pennies|two lepta}}.
Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has given more than all the rest.

L.2: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a certain needy widow putting two lepta there,
L.3: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all [of them].

R.2: He also saw a very poor widow put in {{units:two cents|two lepta}}.
R.3: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you the truth, this poor widow has given more than all those rich people.

decisions.choice: lepta: the smallest coins in use
decisions.reason: A lepton was a tiny copper coin, a hundred and twenty-eighth of a denarius, the day's wage of a laborer (12:59; Mark 12:42). Two of them were almost nothing.

decisions.choice: needy; poor: two words for being poor, the second the stronger
decisions.reason: The narrator calls her needy, someone who has very little. Jesus calls her poor, the word for those who have nothing (6:20). It is the same woman.

decisions.choice: truly: in truth
decisions.reason: Luke has the ordinary word for "truly" here, not the Hebrew word amen, as in 9:27. The force is the same.

decisions.choice: more than all: more than all the others put together
alternatives: more than any one of them
decisions.reason: Jesus measures the gift by what it cost her, as 21:4 explains. Her two coins were more than all the rich gave.

decisions.choice: {{units:two pennies|two lepta}} (B); {{units:two cents|two lepta}} (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the modern smallest coin by default, with the original coin as the alternative, as 12:59 does. Literal keeps the original coin.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
alternatives: In truth I say to you
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering of this formula, as in 4:24.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 21:4
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 21:3-4 are one saying.

records.source: πάντες γὰρ οὗτοι ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ δῶρα, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ὑστερήματος αὐτῆς πάντα τὸν βίον ὃν εἶχεν ἔβαλεν.
records.gloss: All for these out of the abounding to them cast into the gifts, she however out of the lack of her all the livelihood that she had cast.
pieces: Every one of them gave out of their surplus. But she, out of her need, has given the whole of what she had to live on."

L.4: For all these put [gifts] into the offering out of what they had to spare, but she out of her lack put in all the living that she had."

R.4: The rich gave only what they had left over. But she is poor, and she gave all the money she had to live on."

decisions.choice: living: the means of living, what she had to live on
decisions.reason: The word means life in the sense of a livelihood, as in 8:43 and 15:12. She gave everything she had for food and need.

decisions.choice: into the gifts: into the offering, the gifts given to God
alternatives: into the gifts the rich had brought
decisions.reason: The phrase names the offering itself. The gifts went to God through the temple.

decisions.choice: out of her lack: God values a gift by what it costs the giver, not by its size
alternatives: a rebuke of the rich for giving
decisions.reason: Jesus does not blame the rich for giving. He shows what God sees: they kept plenty, and she kept nothing (2 Corinthians 8:12).

decisions.choice: The rich
decisions.reason: Readable names who "all these" are, from 21:1.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: The saying begun in 21:3 ends.

records.source: Καί τινων λεγόντων περὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι λίθοις καλοῖς καὶ ἀναθήμασιν κεκόσμηται εἶπεν·
records.gloss: And some speaking about the temple, that with stones beautiful and offerings it had been adorned, he said,
pieces: Some people were talking about the temple: how fine its stones were, and how it was decorated with gifts given to God. Jesus said,

L.5: And as some were speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with beautiful stones and offerings, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said,

R.5: Some people were talking about the temple. They spoke about how beautiful its stones were, and about the gifts people had given to make it beautiful. Jesus said,

decisions.choice: the temple and its beautiful stones: the temple Herod the Great rebuilt on a grand scale
alternatives: the first temple built by Solomon
decisions.reason: Herod's rebuilding of the temple began about twenty years before Jesus was born and was still going on in his day (John 2:20). It was built of huge, fine stones and was famous for its beauty.

decisions.choice: offerings: gifts dedicated to God and put on display in the temple
decisions.reason: The word means something set up as a gift to God. Such gifts were hung or set up in the temple for people to see. The Jewish historian Josephus describes a golden vine at the entrance of the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: some: people who were there, not named
decisions.reason: Luke does not say who was speaking. In Mark 13:1 it is one of the disciples.

decisions.choice: Jesus said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.heading: Not one stone on another

records.source: Ταῦτα ἃ θεωρεῖτε, ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται λίθος ἐπὶ λίθῳ ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
records.gloss: These things which you are looking at, will come days in which not will be left stone upon stone which not will be thrown down.
pieces: "You are looking at all this. But days are coming when it will all be torn down, and not a stone will stay standing on another."

L.6: "[As for] these things that you are looking at, days will come in which a stone will not be left upon a stone that will not be thrown down."

R.6: "You see all these buildings. But a day is coming when every stone here will be pulled down. Not even two stones will be left one on top of the other."

decisions.choice: the temple will be completely destroyed
decisions.reason: This happened in AD 70, when a Roman army destroyed Jerusalem and burned the temple. Jesus had already wept over the city and said the same of it (19:44).

decisions.choice: these things that you are looking at: a phrase set first for emphasis, with no verb of its own
alternatives: a question: are you looking at these things?
decisions.reason: The phrase stands at the head of the sentence and the rest of the sentence tells what will happen to it.

decisions.choice: You are looking at all this. (B); You see all these buildings. (R)
alternatives: As for these things you are looking at
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the opening phrase a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens and closes in this record
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: Jesus' answer is one sentence.

records.source: Ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;
records.gloss: They asked then him saying, Teacher, when then these things will be, and what the sign when are about these things to take place?
pieces: They put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Teacher, when will these things be? And what sign will there be when they are about to take place?"

L.7: And they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Teacher, when then will these things be, and what [will be] the sign when these things are about to take place?"

R.7: So they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Teacher, when will these things happen? What sign will show us that they are about to happen?"

decisions.choice: sign: a visible event that shows that something is near
decisions.reason: They ask for a sign that will tell them the time. Jesus answers with signs in 21:11 and 21:25.

decisions.choice: these things: the destruction of the temple Jesus has just foretold (21:6)
decisions.reason: The question is about the temple. Jesus' answer runs on from the city's fall to the coming of the Son of Man (21:20-28).

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι καί· Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And he said, Watch out lest you be led astray; many for will come in the name of me saying, I am, and, The time has drawn near; not go after them.
pieces: He answered, "Take care that no one leads you astray. Many will come claiming {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name and saying, 'I am the one!' and, 'The time has come near!' Do not go after them.

L.8: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "See that you are not led astray, for many will come in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, saying, 'I am [he],' and, 'The time has come near.' Do not go after them.

R.8: Jesus said, "Be careful! Do not let anyone fool you. Many people will come and use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. They will say, 'I am the one you are waiting for!' They will say, 'The time has come!' Do not follow them.

decisions.choice: in my name: claiming my name and title for themselves
decisions.reason: They will come as if they were Jesus, or as if they had his authority. The next words show they claim to be the one Israel was waiting for.

decisions.choice: I am: I am he, the one who was promised
decisions.reason: The words are a claim to be the Messiah, the one expected. False leaders of this kind did appear in the years before Jerusalem fell (Acts 5:36-37).

decisions.choice: the time: the time of the end, the time God has set
decisions.reason: The word means a fixed time or season. The false teachers will claim the end has come.

decisions.choice: I am the one you are waiting for!
decisions.reason: Readable says who they claim to be, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 21:9
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: The words of 21:8-9 are one answer. Luke then starts again with "Then he said to them" (21:10).

records.source: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλ’ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.
records.gloss: When then you hear of wars and uprisings, not be terrified; it is necessary for these things to take place first, but not immediately the end.
pieces: When you hear about wars and rebellions, do not panic. All this has to happen first, but it does not mean that the end comes at once."

L.9: And when you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified; for these things must take place first, but the end [is] not immediately."

R.9: You will hear about wars and about people fighting against their rulers. Do not be afraid. These things must happen first. But the end will not come right after them."

decisions.choice: uprisings: revolts, disorder in the land
decisions.reason: The word means unrest and rebellion, people rising against those who rule them.

decisions.choice: must: it is part of God's plan
decisions.reason: The same word is used of what must happen to the Son of Man (9:22). These things do not happen outside God's purpose.

decisions.choice: the end: the end of the age
alternatives: the end of the temple only
decisions.reason: Wars do not mean that the last day has come. There will be more to happen first (21:12, 24).

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: Luke's narration interrupts in 21:10.

records.source: τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπ’ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν, σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι καὶ κατὰ τόπους λιμοὶ καὶ λοιμοὶ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ σημεῖα ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ μεγάλα ἔσται.
records.gloss: Then he was saying to them, Will rise up nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom, \v 11 earthquakes both great and in places famines and plagues there will be, terrors both and signs from heaven great there will be.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on to tell them, "One nation will go to war with another, and one kingdom with another.
There will be powerful earthquakes, and in place after place famines and diseases. Fearful things will happen, and great signs will appear in the sky.

L.10: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom,
L.11: and there will be great earthquakes, and famines and plagues in various places; and there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.

R.10: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Nations will fight against each other. Kingdoms will fight against each other.
R.11: There will be strong earthquakes. In many places people will go hungry and get sick. Terrible things will happen, and there will be great signs in the sky.

decisions.choice: nation will rise against nation: peoples will go to war with one another
decisions.reason: The words echo the prophets' pictures of nations at war (2 Chronicles 15:6; Isaiah 19:2).

decisions.choice: famines and plagues: lack of food and deadly disease
decisions.reason: The two Greek words sound almost the same, and Luke puts them side by side. Hunger and disease often came together.

decisions.choice: from heaven: from the sky
decisions.reason: The word can mean the sky or the place where God is. Here it is where the signs are seen, as in 21:25.

decisions.choice: in the sky
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the signs will be seen, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 21:28
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 21:10-28 are one speech.

records.source: Πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·
records.gloss: Before however these things all they will lay upon you the hands of them and will persecute, delivering to the synagogues and prisons, being led before kings and governors on account of the name of me;
pieces: Before all that, however, they will arrest you and hunt you down. They will hand you over to synagogues and to prisons, and you will be led off to stand before kings and governors for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

L.12: But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute [you], handing [you] over to the synagogues and prisons, [and you will be] led away before kings and governors because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

R.12: But before all this happens, people will grab you and treat you cruelly. They will take you to the synagogues to be judged, and they will put you in prison. They will drag you in front of kings and rulers, because you follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: lay their hands on you: arrest you
decisions.reason: To lay hands on someone is to seize them (20:19; Acts 4:3).

decisions.choice: synagogues: the local Jewish assemblies, which also judged and punished their members
decisions.reason: Synagogue leaders could have a member beaten (Acts 22:19; 2 Corinthians 11:24).

decisions.choice: before kings and governors: as happened to the apostles
decisions.reason: In Acts the apostles are arrested and put on trial, and Paul stands before the governors Felix and Festus and King Agrippa (Acts 4:3; 24-26).

decisions.choice: because of my name: because you belong to me and bear my name
alternatives: because you use my name in magic
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person. They will suffer for being his followers (Acts 5:41).

decisions.choice: to be judged; because you follow me
alternatives: to the synagogues; because of my name
decisions.reason: Readable says why they are taken to the synagogues and what "because of my name" means, as the meaning decisions explain.

records.source: ἀποβήσεται ὑμῖν εἰς μαρτύριον.
records.gloss: It will turn out to you for a testimony.
pieces: This will give you the chance to bear witness.

L.13: This will turn out for you as [an opportunity for] testimony.

R.13: This will be your chance to tell them about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: for a testimony: an opportunity for you to bear witness to Jesus before them
alternatives: evidence against them at the judgment
evidence in your favor at the judgment
decisions.reason: Being put on trial will let them speak about Jesus before rulers, as the next verses go on to say (21:14-15) and as Acts shows. Some read it as a witness against the persecutors, as in 9:5.

decisions.choice: to tell them about me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the testimony is about.

records.source: θέτε οὖν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι, ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν ἅπαντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: Put therefore in the hearts of you not to prepare beforehand to make a defense, \v 15 I for will give you a mouth and wisdom which not will be able to resist or to contradict all those opposing you.
pieces: So settle it in your hearts: do not plan your defense in advance.
I myself will give you the words and the wisdom to speak, and not one of your opponents will be able to stand against them or argue back.

L.14: So set [it] in your hearts not to prepare beforehand how to make a defense,
L.15: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom that none of those who oppose you will be able to withstand or contradict.

R.14: So decide now that you will not plan ahead what to say to defend yourselves.
R.15: I will give you the right words to say. I will make you wise. None of your enemies will be able to stand against you or prove you wrong.

decisions.choice: set it in your hearts: make up your minds, decide firmly
decisions.reason: The heart is where a person thinks and decides. The disciples are to decide ahead of time not to rely on a prepared speech.

decisions.choice: prepare beforehand to make a defense: rehearse a speech of defense before a court
decisions.reason: The verb means to practice or prepare in advance. To make a defense is the word for speaking for oneself at a trial (12:11; Acts 26:1).

decisions.choice: a mouth: words to speak
alternatives: the power to speak at all
decisions.reason: God promised Moses to be with his mouth and teach him what to say (Exodus 4:12).

decisions.choice: I: emphatic: Jesus himself will give them the words
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis. In 12:12 Jesus says the Holy Spirit will teach them; both promises stand together.

decisions.choice: the words (B); the right words to say (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom.

records.source: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν, καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
records.gloss: You will be handed over then even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put to death [some] from you, \v 17 and you will be being hated by all because of the name of me.
pieces: You will be handed over even by your own parents and {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, your relatives and your friends, and some of you they will kill.
You will be hated by everyone on account of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

L.16: And you will be handed over even by parents and {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} and relatives and friends, and they will put [some] of you to death,
L.17: and you will be hated by all because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

R.16: Even your parents, your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, your relatives, and your friends will turn you over to your enemies. They will kill some of you.
R.17: Everyone will hate you because you follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: handed over: given up to the authorities, betrayed
decisions.reason: It is the verb of 21:12 and of Judas giving Jesus up (22:4). Here it is done by one's own family.

decisions.choice: brothers: brothers and sisters, the children of one family
decisions.reason: In this list of family members the plural means the person's own brothers and sisters.

decisions.choice: of you: some of you
decisions.reason: The phrase means a part of the group: not all, but some, will be killed.

decisions.choice: because of my name: because you belong to me
decisions.reason: As in 21:12, the name stands for Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The word means brothers and sisters here, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: because you follow me
decisions.reason: Readable says what "because of my name" means.

records.source: καὶ θρὶξ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται.
records.gloss: And a hair from the head of you not not will perish.
pieces: Yet not a single hair of your head will be lost.

L.18: And not a hair of your head will perish.

R.18: But not even one hair on your head will be destroyed.

decisions.choice: not a hair will perish: you are completely safe in God's keeping, even if you are killed
alternatives: none of you will be harmed or die
decisions.reason: Jesus has just said that some will be put to death (21:16). The promise is about what is lasting: God keeps his people whole (12:4-7; 1 Samuel 14:45 uses the same picture).

decisions.choice: not a hair: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together for an emphatic denial.

records.source: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν κτήσασθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: In the endurance of you gain the lives of you.
pieces: Hold out to the end, and so win your lives.

L.19: By your endurance gain your lives.

R.19: Do not give up! If you keep going, you will win true life.

decisions.choice: gain: a command
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT prints the command. Other important manuscripts, among them Alexandrinus and Vaticanus, have the future, "you will gain". The two forms differ by one letter, and either way the point is that endurance leads to life. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: endurance: staying firm under pressure, not giving up
decisions.reason: The word is used of those who hold on to the word and bear fruit (8:15).

decisions.choice: lives: the true life of the person, life with God
alternatives: souls as a part of a person
decisions.reason: The same word is used where Jesus says that whoever loses his life for him will save it (9:24). Some will lose their lives in this world (21:16) but gain true life.

decisions.choice: Do not give up! If you keep going, you will win true life.
alternatives: By your endurance gain your lives.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the command into two short sentences and says what kind of life is meant, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ στρατοπέδων Ἰερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: When then you see being surrounded by armies Jerusalem, then know that has drawn near the desolation of her.
pieces: When you see Jerusalem with armies encamped all around it, then be sure that it will soon be laid waste.

L.20: But when you see Jerusalem being surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near.

R.20: Some day you will see armies all around Jerusalem. When that happens, you can be sure that the city will soon be destroyed.

decisions.choice: armies: armies in camp, encamped around the city
decisions.reason: The word means an army camp, and so an army in the field.

decisions.choice: its desolation: the city laid waste, as Daniel foretold
alternatives: the city emptied of people only
decisions.reason: The word echoes Daniel's prophecy of a desolation that would come on the city and the sanctuary (Daniel 9:26-27; compare Mark 13:14). Luke says plainly that it means the city's destruction.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem surrounded: fulfilled when Roman armies besieged and took the city in AD 70
alternatives: a siege at the end of history only
decisions.reason: Jesus had already spoken of enemies setting up a siege around the city (19:43). The siege of AD 70 is well known from history.

decisions.choice: know: a command: then be sure
decisions.reason: The form can be a command or a statement. After "then" it reads as a command.

records.heading: Jerusalem surrounded

records.source: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, καὶ οἱ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ἐκχωρείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χώραις μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς αὐτήν, ὅτι ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως αὗταί εἰσιν τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα.
records.gloss: Then those in the Judea let them flee to the mountains, and those in midst of her let them depart out, and those in the countrysides not let them enter into her, \v 22 because days of vengeance these are, of the to be fulfilled all things having been written.
pieces: Then people in Judea should run for the hills. Those inside the city should leave it, and those out in the fields should not go back in.
For these are the days of punishment, when everything that is written will come true.

L.21: Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, and those inside the city must get out, and those in the country must not go into it,
L.22: because these are days of vengeance, for all the things that have been written to be fulfilled.

R.21: Then the people in Judea must run away to the mountains. People in the city must leave it. People out in the country must not go into the city.
R.22: At that time God will punish the city. Everything the Scriptures say will happen.

decisions.choice: her: Jerusalem, not Judea
decisions.reason: Those in Judea are to flee to the hills, those in the city are to leave it, and those outside are not to go into it. The city is the one named in 21:20.

decisions.choice: vengeance: punishment, justice carried out
decisions.reason: The word is used of God's justice on the wicked. The prophets speak of days of punishment coming on Israel (Hosea 9:7; Deuteronomy 32:35).

decisions.choice: all that has been written: the prophets' warnings of judgment on Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The prophets had warned that the city and its temple would fall (Micah 3:12; Jeremiah 7:14; Daniel 9:26).

decisions.choice: inside the city (L, B); in the city (R)
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to Jerusalem, and every level names the city.

decisions.choice: God will punish the city
decisions.reason: Readable names who punishes, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ, καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πάντα, καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι οὗ πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.
records.gloss: Woe to the ones in womb having and to the ones nursing in those the days; will be for distress great upon the land and wrath to the people this, \v 24 and they will fall by mouth of sword and will be led captive into the nations all, and Jerusalem will be being trampled by Gentiles, until that are fulfilled times of Gentiles.
pieces: How terrible it will be in those days for women who are pregnant or nursing a baby! Great hardship will come on the land, and wrath on this people.
They will be cut down by the sword and carried off as captives to every nation. Jerusalem will be trampled underfoot by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles have run their course.

L.23: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing [babies] in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people,
L.24: and they will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by [the] Gentiles until [the] times of [the] Gentiles are fulfilled.

R.23: How terrible it will be in those days for women who are going to have babies, and for mothers who are feeding babies! There will be great trouble in the land. God will be angry with this people and punish them.
R.24: Some will be killed with swords. Others will be taken away as prisoners to every nation. The Gentiles, people who are not Jews, will trample on Jerusalem until the time God has given them is over.

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Israel
decisions.reason: The same word means land or earth. Here the subject is Judea and Jerusalem (21:20-21).

decisions.choice: wrath: God's anger against sin, shown in judgment
decisions.reason: John the Baptist warned of the wrath to come (3:7). Here it falls on "this people", the people of the city that rejected its king (19:41-44).

decisions.choice: mouth of the sword: the edge of the sword
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of speaking of the sword's edge as its mouth (Genesis 34:26).

decisions.choice: the times of the Gentiles: a limited time, set by God, in which the Gentiles rule over Jerusalem
alternatives: the time for the gospel to go to the Gentiles
the time of the Gentiles' own judgment
decisions.reason: The phrase says that Gentile rule over the city has an end that God has fixed. Whether it also means the time in which the good news goes out to the nations (24:47) is debated.

decisions.choice: Woe to (L); How terrible it will be for (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:24-26 and 11:42-52: Literal keeps the old word, and Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews; the time God has given them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word Gentiles and the phrase, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: Καὶ ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου, ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ, αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
records.gloss: And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and upon the earth distress of nations in perplexity at roaring of sea and surge, \v 26 fainting of men from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited world, the for powers of the heavens will be shaken.
pieces: Signs will appear in the sun, the moon and the stars. On the earth whole nations will be gripped with distress, not knowing where to turn as the sea roars and heaves.
Fear will drain the strength out of people as they wait for what is coming on the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

L.25: And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress of nations, in perplexity at the roar of [the] sea and [its] surge,
L.26: people fainting from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited world; for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

R.25: Strange things will happen to the sun, the moon, and the stars. These will be signs. On earth, the nations will be in great trouble. They will be confused and afraid because the sea roars and its waves crash.
R.26: People will be so afraid that they will feel faint. They will wait in fear for what is going to happen to the world. This is because the powers in the sky will be shaken.

decisions.choice: signs in sun, moon and stars: the prophets' pictures of the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of the sun and moon going dark and the stars falling when God comes to judge (Isaiah 13:10; 34:4; Ezekiel 32:7).

decisions.choice: fainting: losing heart and strength, as if the life were going out of them
decisions.reason: The word can mean to faint or even to die. Here it describes people overcome with fear.

decisions.choice: the powers of the heavens: the sun, moon and stars, the heavenly bodies
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 34:4 the host of heaven melts away. Some take the powers to be spiritual beings, but the verse continues the signs in the sky of 21:25.

decisions.choice: the inhabited world: the whole world where people live
decisions.reason: The word means the inhabited earth (2:1; 4:5).

decisions.choice: Strange things will happen to the sun, the moon, and the stars. These will be signs.
alternatives: There will be signs in sun and moon and stars.
decisions.reason: Readable says first what will happen and then names it a sign.

records.heading: The Son of Man comes in a cloud

records.source: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλῃ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς.
records.gloss: And then they will see the Son of the Man coming in a cloud with power and glory great.
pieces: And then people will see the Son of Man come in a cloud with power and with great glory.

L.27: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

R.27: Then people will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud. He will come with power and great glory.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man coming in a cloud: Daniel 7:13-14
alternatives: a new picture without a source
decisions.reason: Daniel saw one like a son of man come with the clouds of heaven and receive authority, glory and a kingdom. Jesus speaks of himself (9:26).

decisions.choice: a cloud: the sign of God's presence
decisions.reason: God's presence went with Israel in a cloud (Exodus 13:21), and a cloud covered the disciples on the mountain (9:34-35). Jesus was taken up in a cloud and will come back in the same way (Acts 1:9-11).

decisions.choice: they: the people of the earth just described
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. It continues from the nations and people of 21:25-26.

decisions.choice: people will see
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who will see, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: Beginning then these things to take place, straighten up and lift up the heads of you, because draws near the redemption of you.
pieces: As soon as these things start to happen, straighten up and look up, for the day of your redemption is almost here."

L.28: And when these things begin to take place, stand up straight and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near."

R.28: When these things start to happen, stand up straight and look up! God is coming soon to set you free."

decisions.choice: redemption: release, being set free by God
decisions.reason: The word comes from the setting free of slaves and captives. Zechariah and Anna spoke of God redeeming his people (1:68; 2:38).

decisions.choice: straighten up and lift your heads: take courage, look up with hope
decisions.reason: People bowed down with fear or shame keep their heads low. The disciples are to look up, because the signs that terrify others mean rescue for them.

decisions.choice: God is coming soon to set you free
decisions.reason: Readable says what redemption is and who brings it, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: The speech begun in 21:10 ends, and Luke's narration starts again in 21:29.

records.source: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·
records.gloss: And he said a parable to them, Look at the fig tree and all the trees;
pieces: He told them a parable: "Look at the fig tree, and at all the trees.

L.29: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them a parable: "Look at the fig tree and all the trees.

R.29: Then Jesus told them a parable, a story with a lesson: "Look at the fig tree and at all the other trees.

decisions.choice: parable: a comparison taken from everyday life
decisions.reason: A parable can be a short comparison, as here, or a story (8:4).

decisions.choice: the fig tree: a tree that loses its leaves in winter and puts out new leaves late in spring
decisions.reason: Fig trees were common in the land. Their new leaves showed that summer was near (Song of Songs 2:13).

decisions.choice: a story with a lesson
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as in 8:4.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 21:36
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 21:29-36 are one speech.

records.heading: Learn from the fig tree

records.source: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
records.gloss: When they put out already, seeing from yourselves you know that already near the summer is;
pieces: Once they burst into leaf, you only need to look at them to know that summer is near.

L.30: When they already put out [leaves], you see [it] and know for yourselves that summer is already near.

R.30: When they start to grow new leaves, you see them, and you know that summer will soon be here.

decisions.choice: for yourselves: without anyone telling you
decisions.reason: Anyone can read the season from the trees. In the same way the disciples will read the signs (21:31).

decisions.choice: [leaves] (L); leaf, leaves (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to put out shoots or leaves. English needs to say what the trees put out.

records.source: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: So also you, when you see these things taking place, know that near is the kingdom of the God.
pieces: It is the same with you. When you see these things happening, be sure of this: the kingdom of God is near.

L.31: So also you, when you see these things taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near.

R.31: It is the same for you. When you see these things happen, you will know that the kingdom of God is coming soon.

decisions.choice: know: a command or a statement; both say the same
decisions.reason: The form can be read either way. The disciples are to recognize what the signs mean.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God is near: God's rule is about to come in its fullness
alternatives: the kingdom has not yet begun at all
decisions.reason: The kingdom was already present in Jesus (17:21). Here it is the kingdom coming in full with the Son of Man (21:27-28).

decisions.choice: these things: the signs Jesus has described
decisions.reason: The comparison applies the lesson of the trees to the signs of 21:25-28.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you that not not will pass away the generation this until all things take place.
pieces: Truly I tell you, all of this will happen before this generation is gone.

L.32: Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all [these things] take place.

R.32: I tell you the truth, the people of this generation will not all die before all these things happen.

decisions.choice: Truly: a Hebrew word (amen) that confirms what follows
decisions.reason: Jesus uses amen to introduce his own words with authority, as in 4:24.

decisions.choice: this generation: the people living in Jesus' day
alternatives: the Jewish people through the ages
the generation that sees the final signs
decisions.reason: In Luke "this generation" means Jesus' own contemporaries (7:31; 11:29-32, 50-51; 17:25). On this reading "all" includes what the disciples asked about, the fall of the temple (21:6-7), which came within forty years. Others take the phrase in one of the wider senses, because the coming of the Son of Man is still awaited.

decisions.choice: certainly not: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together for an emphatic denial.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering, as in 4:24.

decisions.choice: all of this will happen before this generation is gone
alternatives: this generation will not pass away until all takes place
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the double negative into a plain statement with the same meaning.

records.source: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
records.gloss: The heaven and the earth will pass away, the but words of me not not will pass away.
pieces: Heaven and earth will disappear, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will last forever.

L.33: Heaven and earth will pass away, but {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words will certainly not pass away.

R.33: The sky and the earth will not last forever. But what I say will last forever.

decisions.choice: my words will not pass away: Jesus' words last as God's own word does
alternatives: his words will be remembered by people
decisions.reason: The prophets say that the word of God stands forever while all else fades (Isaiah 40:8; 51:6). Jesus says the same of his own words.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth: the whole created world
alternatives: the place of God and the place of people
decisions.reason: The pair names everything God made (Genesis 1:1).

decisions.choice: certainly not: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together for an emphatic denial.

decisions.choice: will last forever
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the strong negative in a positive way.

decisions.choice: what I say
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase.

records.source: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε βαρηθῶσιν ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ἐπιστῇ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη ὡς παγίς· ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: Take heed then to yourselves lest be weighed down of you the hearts with carousing and drunkenness and cares of life, and come upon you suddenly the day that \v 35 as a trap; it will come in for upon all those sitting upon face of all the earth.
pieces: Be on your guard. Do not let your hearts grow dull with wild parties and drinking and the worries of everyday life, or that day will catch you off guard,
like a trap that snaps shut. It will come on everyone who lives anywhere on earth.

L.34: But watch yourselves, so that your hearts are not weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the cares of life, and that day comes upon you suddenly
L.35: like a trap; for it will come upon all who live on the face of the whole earth.

R.34: Be careful! Do not let wild parties, drinking too much, or worrying about this life fill up your thoughts. If you do, that day will come on you when you do not expect it,
R.35: like a trap that catches an animal. That day will come to everyone who lives on the earth.

decisions.choice: carousing: wild drinking and its after-effects
decisions.reason: The word is used of the headache and sickness after a night of drinking, and so of drunken revelry itself.

decisions.choice: hearts weighed down: made dull and heavy, not alert to God
decisions.reason: A heavy heart here is one made sluggish by pleasure or worry, like the seed choked by worries and pleasures (8:14).

decisions.choice: that day: the day the Son of Man comes
decisions.reason: Jesus has spoken of the day of the Son of Man (17:24-30). The next verse says it will come on the whole earth.

decisions.choice: like a trap: suddenly, without warning
decisions.reason: Isaiah warns of terror, pit and snare coming on those who live on the earth (Isaiah 24:17).

decisions.choice: sitting on the face of the whole earth: living anywhere on earth
decisions.reason: To sit is a Hebrew way of saying to live in a place (Jeremiah 25:29).

decisions.choice: worries (B); worrying (R); cares (L)
decisions.reason: As in 12:22-26, Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

records.heading: Stay awake and pray

records.source: ἀγρυπνεῖτε δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
records.gloss: Keep awake then in every time praying that you may have strength to escape these things all the things being about to take place, and to stand before the Son of the Man.
pieces: Keep watch at all times, and pray for strength to come safely through all that is going to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man."

L.36: But stay awake at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to take place, and to stand before the Son of Man."

R.36: Always be ready, and keep praying. Pray that God will make you strong enough to get through all these things that are going to happen. Pray that you will be able to stand in front of the Son of Man without fear."

decisions.choice: you may have strength
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "have strength", with Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other early manuscripts. Alexandrinus, Bezae and most later manuscripts read "be counted worthy", the reading of the Textus Receptus, the Greek text printed in the sixteenth century. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: stay awake: be alert and watchful
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep from sleeping, and so to stay alert, like slaves waiting for their master (12:35-40).

decisions.choice: escape: come safely through
decisions.reason: Disciples will suffer (21:12-17). To escape is to come through these things without falling away.

decisions.choice: to stand before the Son of Man: to be approved by him when he comes to judge
decisions.reason: To stand in the judgment is to be accepted by the judge (Psalm 1:5; Malachi 3:2).

decisions.choice: God will make you strong; without fear
alternatives: you may have strength; to stand
decisions.reason: Readable names who gives strength and says what standing before the Son of Man means, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
alternatives: a separate quotation for each sentence
decisions.reason: The speech begun in 21:29 ends.

records.source: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν·
records.gloss: He was now the days in the temple teaching, the and nights going out he was lodging on the mountain the [one] called of Olives;
pieces: By day Jesus was teaching in the temple. At night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would go out of the city and spend the night on the hill known as the Mount of Olives.

L.37: Now during the days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching in the temple, and at night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out and spent the night on the mountain called [the Mount] of Olives.

R.37: Every day Jesus taught in the temple. Every night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left the city and stayed on the Mount of Olives.

decisions.choice: lodged: spent the night, perhaps in the open
decisions.reason: The verb means to spend the night. Jesus and the disciples went to the Mount of Olives as their custom (22:39); Mark 11:11 says they went out to Bethany, on the same hill.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the hill east of Jerusalem, across the Kidron valley
decisions.reason: Jesus came down this hill when he entered the city (19:29, 37).

decisions.choice: Jesus; out of the city, left the city
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus and say where he went out from.

records.source: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And all the people were rising early to him in the temple to hear him.
pieces: At dawn all the people would come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the temple to listen.

L.38: And all the people would come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} early in the morning in the temple to hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.38: All the people got up early each morning and came to the temple to listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: come early: get up at dawn to come
decisions.reason: The verb means to rise early in the morning. The people came at first light.

decisions.choice: the chapter ends here
alternatives: the story of the woman caught in adultery follows
decisions.reason: A group of later manuscripts places the story of the woman caught in adultery (John 7:53-8:11) after this verse. It is not part of Luke in the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.
